rogue.role: Finishes weak foes, bleeds the rest

paladin.role: Hits, heals and holds the line

druid.role: Poisons foes, grows the party back

tinker.role: Gadgets, turrets and spare ink for friends

shaman.role: Totems that power the party, lightning that jumps

telepath.role: Psychic healer: reads minds, freezes foes, mends friends

bard.role: Songs that power, heal and refill the party

ranger.role: Arrows that find weak spots from afar

monk.role: Flurries of hits, calm healing, hard to touch

dragoon.role: Leaps from the sky onto the strongest foe

summoner.role: Calls storybook beasts for huge spells

chrono.role: Bends time: rewinds friends, stops foes

alchemist.role: Potions for friends, poison for foes

dancer.role: Dizzying steps, party dodges, fast hits

mimic.role: Learns foes’ tricks, a bit of everything

passenger.role: A rogue who lets an inner shadow drive
passenger.mech: Shadow moves wake the Passenger: +12% damage per stack, up to 5. At 3 or more it may take over and pick its own move and target. The Code settles it.

regency.role: Wit, rumor and etiquette as weapons
regency.mech: Snubs and rumors fluster foes so they hit 30% softer. Etiquette obliges foes to move into her lane, so the party can reach them.
regency.book: Pride and Prejudice and the other novels of Jane Austen

coinshot.role: Leaps between lanes, fires coins like bullets
coinshot.mech: Steelpush moves launch it into the lane of the foe it attacks, so it can strike any foe anywhere. Ironpull drags a foe into its lane.

burner.role: A gritty sapper with explosives and pure spite
burner.mech: Spite: below half health it hits 30% harder. Its munitions blow foes out of cover, leaving them exposed.
burner.book: Malazan Book of the Fallen, by Steven Erikson

windrunner.role: Lashes gravity to fight from any lane and pin foes
windrunner.mech: Lashings launch it into the lane of the foe it strikes, and Gravitation pins foes to the floor so they can’t act. Protects first: its oath shields the party.
windrunner.book: The Stormlight Archive, by Brandon Sanderson

dunadan.role: Tracks, hides, heals with herb lore and poisons foes
dunadan.mech: A tracker and healer: its marks expose foes, its blades poison them, and athelas heals the whole party and clears bad effects.
dunadan.book: The Lord of the Rings, by J.R.R. Tolkien

TQ_META.d: Revive the party once per tale

says: Achoo! Did I get dust on you?
Nobody has cleaned under this shelf in YEARS.
Snip snip! Hold still.
I love the sound of a fresh page.
Splotch! You look better smudged.
I spread. It’s what I do.
Want to know how it ends?
I know a secret about chapter nine…
I have nothing to say. That’s the point.
You are ninety-nine years late.
Fines! Fines for everyone!
Fall in. Everyone does eventually.
Where did that chapter go? Inside me.
Teh end is neer!
I put a typo in your name. Hehe.
Munch munch. Tastes like a classic.
I only eat the good parts.
And then… you’ll never know!
To be continued… FOREVER.
Oops. That will never come out.
Who leaves a mug on a library book? Me.
Shhhhhh.
Silence in the stacks.
And then and then and then and then
I never stop, I never pause, I never
That’s a comma splice.
Your adventure needs a red pen.
I’m just a book. A normal book. Open me.
Wrong shelf, right snack.
Read the small print, did you?
Terms apply. Mostly to you.
Ooh, shiny bookmark! Mine.
Finders keepers.
Running down the hall, the book was chased.
Who is doing what? Exactly.
Stick around!
Two pages, one page, who can tell?
Someone read me in the bath.
Drip. Drip. Drip.

says: Off with their heads!
Who painted these roses?

TQ_BOSS.say: A different side of the doctor…
says: A different side of the doctor…
The doctor is OUT.

TQ_BOSS.say: A web of perfectly planned plots.
says: A web of perfectly planned plots.
Every move you make, I planned last week.

TQ_BOSS.n: The Wicked Witch of the West

says: I’ll get you, my pretty!
Fly, my pretties!

TQ_BOSS.say: Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!
says: Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!
Arr, that be my treasure map.

TQ_BOSS.say: Beware the bridge at midnight…
says: Beware the bridge at midnight…
Lend me your head, would you?

TQ_BOSS.say: Such a cold, clear heart.
says: Such a cold, clear heart.
Let your heart freeze, just a little.

TQ_BOSS.say: Beware the jaws that bite, the claws that catch!
says: Beware the jaws that bite, the claws that catch!
Burble, burble!

TQ_BOSS.say: The jungle remembers who belongs here.
says: The jungle remembers who belongs here.
Run, little cub.

TQ_BOSS.say: Guess my name, little readers!
says: Guess my name, little readers!
You will never, ever guess it.

TQ_BOSS.say: Everything has a price, darling.
says: Everything has a price, darling.
Sign right here, sweetheart.

TQ_BOSS.say: You can’t fight what you can’t see.
says: You can’t fight what you can’t see.
Over here. No, over here.

TQ_BOSS.say: Bah! Every one of you owes me ink.
says: Bah! Every one of you owes me ink.

says: Too much singing in this hall!
QUIET!

TQ_BOSS.say: Sing for me!
says: Sing for me!
The music of the night is mine.

Into the pot, little dumplings.

says: It takes all the running you can do to stay in place!
Faster! FASTER!

TQ_DARK.say: Every story ends blank. I simply hurry it along.
says: Hold still. You’re smudging.
I’ll leave you a lovely empty page.
TQ_DARK.want: every last page in every book is fading to white

TQ_DARK.say: Some words are simply… not for you.
says: That part of your story? ███████.
I decide which chapters you read.
TQ_DARK.want: whole chapters are vanishing under thick black bars

TQ_DARK.say: I have never finished a book. Neither will you.
says: Why read when you could… stop?
Your bookmark is slipping.
TQ_DARK.want: readers everywhere are forgetting how their stories end

TQ_DARK.say: Your story? I wrote it. Badly. On purpose.
says: Plot hole! Fall in it!
I’m giving you a terrible sequel.
TQ_DARK.want: heroes in every book are being rewritten into villains

TQ_DARK.say: Shall I tell you how this ends? You lose.
says: The butler did it. Also, you lose.
I’ve read ahead. It’s bad for you.

TQ_DARK.say: You are overdue. Very, very overdue.
says: That will be a fine. A very fine fine.
Your library card has been… revoked.
TQ_DARK.want: library books are disappearing into his endless return slot

says: Find out next time! Except there isn’t one.
Every chapter ends on a ledge.
TQ_DARK.lair: the Edge of Page Four Hundred
TQ_DARK.want: stories are stopping halfway, mid-sentence, forever

TQ_DARK.say: Drip. Drip. Every page turns black eventually.
says: I’m in the margins. I’m in the gutters.
You can’t wash me out.
TQ_DARK.want: a black stain is spreading through every library

knight: Nice armor. Is it cardboard?
A knight? In a library? How quaint.
Your shield has a dog-ear, {p}.
Clank, clank, here comes the tin can.
Hardcover, are we? I chew hardcovers.
Oh look, the bookend thinks it’s a hero.
That helmet won’t keep the plot out.
So you’re the one guarding the shelf.
Polish that shield all you like.
Brave little bookend, aren’t you?
I’ve seen sturdier pop-up books.
I’ll bend your spine and leave you on the bargain shelf.
By the last page, you’ll be a paperback.
Even castles crumble when the ink runs dry.
Your oath ends at the next full stop.
I’ll stamp you overdue and lose you in the stacks.
Stand still so I can crease you properly.
Nobody reads about the knight who lost.
I’ll rewrite you as a footnote.
Charge all you like. The story is mine now.
This chapter has no room for heroes.
scholar: Put down the books, nerd.
All that reading and still no muscles.
Your glasses are fogging up, {p}.
Oh, a scholar. Do you bite, or just cite?
Another bookworm who thinks it’s clever.
How many chapters did you skip to get here?
I’ve eaten encyclopedias bigger than you.
Footnotes won’t save you.
You smell like old paper and homework.
Quiet in the stacks, little scholar.
Look who brought a bibliography to a brawl.
I’ll smudge every page you ever learned.
There’s no answer key for this.
Class is dismissed, permanently.
Your thesis ends here.
I’ll scramble your index till you can’t find your own name.
Study this: you lose.
This is a pop quiz, and you’re failing.
I’ll spill ink all over your notes.
Even a {g} story has a final exam.
Let’s see if your library card covers this.
trick: I know a cheap trick when I see one.
A plot twist with legs. Adorable.
Keep your paws where I can see them.
You talk fast for someone so small.
Let’s see you twist out of this one.
No sleight of hand gets past me.
Your luck just ran out of pages.
I’ll press you flat like a flower in a dictionary.

The audience is leaving, and so are you.
Run all you want. The margins are mine.
I’ll fold you into a paper crane.
healer: Aww, the tea kettle came to fight.
A healer? How cozy. How weak.
Bring a blanket, {p}? You’ll need it.
Patching friends up won’t patch this.
Look, it’s the nurse of naptime.
What’s in the cup? Courage?
You smell like cocoa and fear.
Fluffing pillows won’t stop me.
Such a soft little helper.
Your bandages are showing.
Did you bring enough tea for everyone?
I’ll spill your tea and blame you.
Your friends will run out of hugs before I run out of mean.
Bedtime is coming, and you won’t like this story.
I’ll turn your lullaby into a screech.
No cozy chapter can save them now.
I’ll cancel naptime forever.
Heal all you like. I hit harder.
Your kettle is about to boil over.
I’ll steal every blanket in this story.
Even happy endings get torn out.
sleuth: Put the magnifying glass away, snoop.
Another detective? I’ve hidden from better.
You’ll never find my weak spot.
Ask one more question. I dare you.
Got a clue? Didn’t think so.
There’s no case to crack here.
That trench coat is three sizes too big.
Sniffing around my chapter, are you?
This mystery ends with you in the lost and found.
The last clue leads straight to your defeat.
I’ll hide you where nobody ever looks: the instruction manual.
Your hunch is wrong this time.
No witnesses, no heroes, no sequel.
In this {g} story, the detective disappears.
Search all you like. The ending is locked.
rogue: A rogue in a library? Bold.
I’ll put you back on the bargain shelf.
You’ll be a footnote by sunset.
mage: Oh no, a spellcaster. How scary.
Nice robe. Is that a bathrobe?
I read the spoilers. You lose.
Your mana pool is a puddle.
Try a cantrip, it might tickle.
Your spellbook has a coffee stain.
I counter your spell with my face.
druid: You have leaves in your fur.
Your garden is full of weeds.
Go back to your mushroom circle.
Nature called. It wants a refund.
tinker: Did you build that from a kit?
Have you tried turning it off and on?
Your robot has a loose screw.
Nice prototype. Shame about the bugs.
shaman: Your thunder is a tummy rumble.
Partly cloudy with a chance of defeat.
telepath: My mind is a locked library.
I’m thinking about winning. Read that.
You can’t lift me, I’m heavy with evil.
Your powers come from a cereal box.
bard: No one asked for an encore.
I’ve heard better from a squeaky door.
ranger: Nice bow. Is it a coat hanger?
Ranger? More like danger. To yourself.
warlock: I read the terms and conditions.
The fees are due, and so are you.
Even shadows think you’re too much.
Your curse is just a typo.
Black nail polish won’t save you.
monk: Om nom nom, I eat monks.
You fight like a library whisper.
ghost: I ain’t afraid of no ghost.
dragoon: Too scared to stay on the ground?
Do you even have a dragon?
I’ll be gone before you land.
You’re all jump and no plan.
summoner: Call your mom while you’re at it.
Gotta catch you all, I mean, beat you all.
Leave a message after the defeat.
chrono: Are you from the future? Sad.
You’re a paradox and a problem.
alchemist: I’m immune, I’ve been licking books.
samurai: You’re a haiku. Short and sad.
dancer: The judges give you a two.
pirate: Your treasure map is a menu.
No rum, no fun, no win.
passenger: You’re very tidy for a hero.
I see the shadow behind you.
regency: Not ten thousand a year, I see.
You’d never be asked to dance.
I shall not be cut by a pet.
coinshot: Nice coins. Spend them on a better plan.
I wear no metal. Good luck.
The Lord Ruler sends his regards.
You’ll run out of coins first.
burner: I’m a god. You’re a sapper.
windrunner: Your oath is a sticky note.
I stand on the ground. Like a grown-up.

knight: Stand behind me, friends!
Hold the line!
For the realm of readers!
Hah!
My shield is bound in oak and promises.
A knight keeps every bookmark safe.
Not one page shall fall today.
You picked the wrong shelf, {f}.
I swore an oath on chapter one.
Steady now.
By the spine of every hardcover!
This shield has stopped worse than you.
I’ll guard this story to the very last line.
Come closer and meet my bookend.
Cardboard? Knock and find out.
Every dent is a chapter I won.
The party walks home, and you walk out.
Lower your voice. This is a library.
I don’t bend, I don’t fold, and I’m never returned late.
You’ll be shelved under Defeated Villains.
My armor is stitched with happy endings.
scholar: Actually, that’s incorrect.
Fascinating. Truly.
I’ve checked my notes.
Let me consult chapter twelve.
Pop quiz!
Ahem.
I’ve read about villains like you.
Correction noted.
Hold on, I’m taking notes.
By the great Library of Everywhere!
Elementary reading, really.
You’re a plot device, and I know how those end.
This is the part where the heroes win.
Your weakness is listed in the appendix.
Knowledge is the heaviest book I carry.
I’ve memorized every move you’re about to make.
The answer is us. Please show your work.
Your plan has a typo in it.
I cite my sources, and my source is victory.
I outnumber you in vocabulary alone.
This tome weighs four pounds, and it’s headed your way.
trick: I already swapped your ending with mine.
I picked your pocket while you were monologuing.
This whole battle was a rehearsal.
I tied your shoelaces two chapters ago.
Your best line? I stole it.
The real trick is that I’m having fun.
I’m the twist you didn’t read coming.
I hid a whoopee cushion in your lair.
Blink and you’ll miss the punchline.
Every page I turn, you get dizzier.
healer: Oh dear.
Now, now.
Deep breaths, everyone.
Sweetie, no.
I’ve brought snacks.
Hush now.
Bless your heart.
Kettle’s on!
Everybody gets a hug.
Not on my watch.
Gentle, but firm.
Someone needs a nap, and it’s you.
My tea has fixed worse days than this.
I’ll patch up my friends faster than you can scratch them.
Cozy is a superpower, actually.
I have a blanket with your name on it. It says Defeated.
You’re grumpy because you skipped your bedtime story.
A warm cup and a brave heart beat you any day.
Kindness hits harder than you think.
Go sit in the quiet corner and think about it.
Everyone here gets a happy ending except you.
sleuth: You blink twice before every attack.
You have ink on your paws. Guilty.
Your weak spot is on the left, and I’m aiming there.
Your alibi has a plot hole in it.
I solved you before you walked in.
The butler didn’t do it. You did.
I followed your muddy footprints all the way here.
You’re hiding a soft side, and I found it.
I’ll put you on the shelf of solved cases.
rogue: Your coin purse is lighter, by the way.
I read the last page first.
Every shadow is a bookmark to me.
I’m the plot twist you didn’t see.
Tell me you’re a villain without telling me.
Rogues don’t fight fair. We fight interesting.
mage: I cast Magic Missile at the darkness.
A wizard is never late. You are early to losing.
My spellbook has a whole chapter on you.
That’s not a crit. THIS is a crit.
Ten out of ten, would fireball again.
paladin: By the Light of the reading lamp!
Faith, trust and a little bookmark dust.
My shield is polished with kindness.
I heal my friends and I smite my problems.
A paladin always finishes the book.
druid: Every leaf is a page I protect.
The roots go deeper than your plot.
tinker: It’s not a bug, it’s a feature!
I have a gadget for that.
I built this in a cave! With a box of scraps!
shaman: Earth, wind and fire, and also me.
Bloodlust! Wait, wrong button. Still works.
telepath: I already know your next move, {f}.
I’m reading you like a paperback.
You were going to say that.
I moved the bookshelf. With my mind.
I can hear you plotting. It’s cringe.
Your plan just left your head and entered mine.
bard: I’m not throwing away my shot!
One more time, from the top!
This is my eleven o’clock number.
ranger: They’re taking the villains to Isengard!
I aimed for your plot hole.
That arrow had your name on it. Literally.
Trees are my cover, books are my life.
Down the middle, like a good bookmark.
I can do this all day.
warlock: Sign here. And here. And here.
Fear me. Or don’t. I’m busy.
Your health looks better on me.
I never return books. Or mercy.
That’s a late fee you can’t pay.
monk: You are already beaten. You just don’t know it yet.
I read in total silence. You lose in it.
The library thanks you for your quiet defeat.
ghost: I have unfinished business. It’s you.
Your story ends here. I would know.
Try hitting what you can’t see.
I’m the ghost of chapters past.
dragoon: I’ve been in the air the whole time.
Floor is lava? I live on the ceiling.
Watch the sky, not the page.
summoner: My friends are bigger than yours.
You fight one of us, you fight all of us.
chrono: Time is relative. So is your victory.
I’m a traveler with a box of books.
I’ll be back. I’ve already been back.
Rule one: the hero never loses.
alchemist: That potion was green. Should’ve been purple.
I measure twice and splash once.
Chemistry is just cooking for heroes.
Gold from lead, wins from losses.
You’ve been transmuted into a loser.
Do not drink. Unless you’re my friend.
samurai: I’ve trained ten thousand pages for this.
dancer: I’m the main character of this dance floor.
Shall we dance? Too late, we are.
mimic: I learn from the best. And from you.
Imitation is the sincerest form of beating you.
I cite my sources in battle.
Your move looks better on me.
I’ve read your whole bestiary entry.
pirate: This is the day you’ll always remember as the day you almost caught a pirate.
Treasure is a story with a happy ending.
Not all treasure is gold. Some is ink.
The sea of stories is mine.
passenger: It’s nothing personal. Just the Code.
The quiet voice says you’re next.
regency: It is a truth universally acknowledged that you will lose, {f}.
My good opinion, once lost, is lost forever.
I dearly love a laugh. Mostly at you.
I shall write about this in a letter.
coinshot: I survived. That’s what I do.
burner: I’ve outlived gods ruder than you.
windrunner: I will protect those who cannot protect themselves.
Honor is not dead while we live.
I fell up just to say hi.
dunadan: All that is gold does not glitter, {f}.
Not all who wander are lost.
A day may come when we fall. It is not this day.
I walk the wild so you can read in peace.
The crownless again shall be king.
I am no stranger to dark places.

ambush: They struck from hiding. Foes hit 15% harder.
swarm: More foes, but each one is smaller.
shield: Every foe starts behind a shield.
worn: More foes, already hurt from another fight.

{n} can now juggle {x}.
{n} stands a little taller today.
{n} learned to read {x} upside down.
{n} has started keeping a battle journal.
{n} tied a tiny bookmark to its tail for luck.
{n} practiced footwork until the moon came out.
{n} now sneezes sparkles when excited.
{n} can sense {x} from across the road.
{n} has a new favorite victory pose.
{n} trained all night with {x}.
{n} earned a nod from the gym leaders.
{n} tells brave stories at the campfire now.
{n} hasn’t tripped over a root in days.
{n} can carry {x} without breaking a sweat.
Villagers point at {n} and whisper “that’s the one”.
{n} sleeps with one eye on the next adventure.
{n} found courage hidden between the pages.
{n} moves like a plot twist.
Foes on the Bramble Road check if {n} is around.
{n} beat {x} in a staring contest.
{n} can tell a good book by its smell.

passenger.strike: Blood work by day. Something quieter by night.
passenger.dp_listen: It never shouts. It doesn’t need to.
passenger.dp_code: Harry’s rules: be careful, be sure, be good at pretending.
passenger.dp_spatter: Every pattern tells a story, if you know how to read it.
passenger.dp_stalk: Miami is so pretty under the moon.
passenger.ult: The car door opens and the Passenger takes the wheel.
passenger.ult2: Tonight is the night. It always is.

regency.strike: Said with a smile, which made it worse.
regency.ri_cut: She looked straight through them, as if they were a draft.
regency.ri_dance: One cannot refuse a dance without causing a scene.
regency.ri_rumor: By Tuesday the whole of Meryton knew.
regency.ri_wit: She dearly loved a laugh, especially at a villain.
regency.ri_call: Tea at four. Gossip at five past.
regency.ult: Every eligible villain in the county, summoned to one ballroom.
regency.ult2: In want of a good beating, apparently.

coinshot.strike: Clink. The cheapest weapon in Luthadel.
coinshot.cs_push: Find the nearest nail and fall sideways off it.
coinshot.cs_volley: A coin is only a coin until a Coinshot throws it.
coinshot.cs_anchor: Push off one coin, aim with another.
coinshot.cs_pull: Buckles, buttons, a belt: all handles.
coinshot.ult: The mists fill with spinning metal.
coinshot.ult2: There’s always another spire to push from.

burner.strike: Not pretty. Gets the job done.
burner.bb_smoke: Smokers are for running. Bridgeburners prefer not to.
burner.bb_burn: Handle with care. Or don’t, and run.
burner.bb_crack: Where there was cover, now there is a hole.
burner.bb_dig: A soldier’s best friend is a deep hole.
burner.bb_sharp: Small enough to throw, mean enough to matter.
burner.ult: The sappers call it the cusser. The enemy calls it nothing, afterward.
burner.ult2: Spite has kept stranger soldiers standing.

windrunner.strike: A bridgeman’s spear, older than the oaths.
windrunner.wr_pin: Stick them to the stone and let them think about it.
windrunner.wr_storm: Light rises from the skin like smoke.
windrunner.wr_sky: The ceiling makes a fine floor.
windrunner.ult: Ride the highstorm. Don’t let it ride you.
windrunner.ult2: The blade is a friend who chose to be a sword.

dunadan.dn_track: A bent blade of grass. A pebble turned over. There.
dunadan.dn_venom: Bitter herbs from the wild lands.
dunadan.dn_athelas: The hands of the king are the hands of a healer.
dunadan.dn_hide: An elven cloak, grey as twilight.
dunadan.dn_ambush: They never saw the Rangers. Nobody ever does.
dunadan.ult: The crownless again shall be king.
dunadan.ult2: Reforged from the shards of Narsil.

TQ_BOONS.d: Once per battle, survive a knockout with 1 HP
When a foe falls, the party gains 1 ink
Heal 4% at the start of each turn

pigs.act: build a brick wall around everyone
pigs.say: Not by the hair of our chinny-chin-chins!
pigs.camp: The three little pigs arrive with a wheelbarrow of bricks and build the sturdiest campfire ring you have ever seen.

mice.act: scurry through the foes, nibbling ankles
mice.camp: Three mice in dark glasses feel their way into camp, holding tails, and share their cheese.

ginger.act: dash between the foes until they are dizzy
ginger.say: Run, run, as fast as you can!
ginger.camp: The Gingerbread Man sprints through camp three times before anyone can say hello.

puss.act: leap in with a flourish of the sword
puss.camp: Puss in Boots bows at the edge of the firelight and tells the tale of his master, the Marquis.

tortoise.act: teach everyone to go slow and steady
tortoise.say: Slow and steady wins the race.
tortoise.camp: The tortoise arrives at camp last, but very calm, and everyone sleeps better for it.

red.act: share a basket of goodies meant for Grandma
red.say: What big teeth you have! Here, have a muffin.
red.camp: Little Red Riding Hood stops by on her way to Grandma’s and leaves a basket of muffins.

humpty.act: have a great fall, right onto a foe
humpty.say: When I use a word, it means just what I choose!
humpty.camp: Humpty Dumpty sits on a log by the fire, wobbling, and explains what every word means.

cheshire.act: grin until the foes forget their guard
cheshire.camp: A grin appears above the campfire, then a cat around it, then only the grin again.

rabbit.camp: The White Rabbit races through camp, checks his watch, and leaves a little early for everyone.

hatter.act: pour everyone a very strange cup of tea
hatter.say: Why is a raven like a writing desk?
hatter.camp: The Mad Hatter sets out a tea table that is far too long and insists it is someone’s unbirthday.

goose.camp: Mother Goose flaps down by the fire and recites rhymes until every pet is smiling.

duckling.act: spread new swan wings and lift everyone up
duckling.say: I never dreamed of such happiness!
duckling.camp: A shy grey duckling shelters by your fire. By morning, it is a swan.

robin.act: loose a volley of arrows from the trees
robin.camp: Robin Hood strolls in from the dark with a sack of stolen snacks for the poor and hungry.

tin.act: stand in front of everyone like a tin wall
tin.say: Now I know I have a heart, because it is breaking.
tin.camp: The Tin Woodman asks for a drop of oil, then stands guard all night without blinking.

lion.act: find his courage and let out a mighty roar
lion.camp: The Cowardly Lion jumps at every crackle of the fire, but he stays, and that is very brave.

peter.act: raid a garden and share the spoils
peter.camp: Peter Rabbit wriggles into camp with radishes stuffed in his jacket and one shoe missing.

tink.act: sprinkle fairy dust on anyone who fell
tink.camp: A tiny light zips around the camp, jingling, and everyone dreams of flying.

toad.act: drive his motorcar straight through the foes
toad.camp: Mr. Toad roars into camp in a motorcar, boasts until midnight, and drives off into a hedge.

bears.act: share porridge that is just right
bears.camp: The Three Bears share three bowls of porridge: one too hot, one too cold, and one just right.

pino.act: tell a whopper so big his nose pokes a foe
pino.say: I am telling the truth! Mostly!
pino.camp: Pinocchio swears he has never told a lie, and his nose knocks the kettle off the fire.

WILD_TIERS.sub: Tall grass, wandering foes, and the way to the caves
Falling leaves, thicker woods and meaner foes
Bog pools, fireflies, and storybook villains as elites
Snowfall, frozen pools and frost-bitten elites
The hardest stretch. Embers drift and villains hunt in packs
